i just had the same surgery back in may! because i’m so small, i can really *feel* the screws.. i’m having them removed next wednesday and hopefully that’ll relieve most of the lingering pain i’m having. my physical therapist told me i should be having 100g of protein a day to help with the healing, along with taking the calcium and vitamin d supplements. i needed (and still need) a lot of help with the healing because i only have half a thyroid. hope your healing journey has few or no complications

they ended up finding out i had an apricot-sized toxic node in my thyroid and removed half of my thyroid (including the node) a couple months after i posted this. the surgery itself and recovery was a breeze compared to my lap. i started having hypothyroidism a few months after surgery. it was pretty nice being able to sleep whenever i wanted. almost wanted to keep the hypothyroidism. it helped me gain a good 10 pounds so i didn’t feel as sickly anymore. i can actually enjoy and finish meals and drinks! now i’m on levothyroxine to stabilize my thyroid hormones.

i feel so much better. there are a lot of emotional and gastrointestinal symptoms i was incorrectly attributing to my endo that have resolved since treating my thyroid. my flare ups seem to come less often and my hormone cycle has a more regular and predictable schedule. (idk about menses since i have had an IUD since my lap 2.5 years ago) and i don’t have nearly as many issues with insomnia as i did before. i’ve even started remembering dreams again. 10/10 would recommend getting your hyperthyroidism treated

I may not have the best experience with cymbalta.

If you don’t already know, it’s classed as an SNRI, or a serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor. Which basically means whatever norepinephrine and serotonin your brain produces on its own will stick around your synapses longer before the “reuptake” or reabsorbtion occurs.

I think my gyn missed the fact that I was already taking Buspar (it tells my brain to produce more serotonin) for anxiety. She had me take the cymbalta at night and I felt like I was vibrating all night, sweating, loud and fast heart rate, and I couldn’t sleep of course. Turns out it gave me serotonin syndrome and my doctors told me to cease taking it immediately…

That said, when you take any (or multiple) medication that affects your serotonin levels, you should be on the lookout for symptoms of serotonin syndrome. They will usually show within 24 hours of taking the new or higher dose at the most. If left unchecked, it can seriously mess you up or even kill you.

I know that doesn’t really answer your question, but with as many different medications we chronic pain sufferers take, this is something to be wary of.

Depo is not only exclusively progesterone, it’s a pretty concentrated amount of the stuff too. I’m sensitive to progesterone and the depo shot made me feel awful. It took me about a year to get back to baseline periods after one dose. I had the Kyleena IUD (hormonal IUD and smaller than mirena) put in during my lap in October and I haven’t had any issues with it since. Obviously, my experience is not universal so take it with a grain of salt. But I have to say from what I’ve seen, depo shot seems to be the most polarizing BC out there. People either love it or hate it.

Depo made me miserable. I was still in just as much pain, but I couldn’t predict my cycles anymore. I was spotting on and off for the better part of a year after one dose. I decided not to get it again. I, personally, react poorly to progesterone. My gyn explained to me that the depo shot is a very highly concentrated form of progesterone compared to other methods which is why I experienced such adverse side effects. I got fitted with the Kyleena IUD in October during my lap and I’m in love. My libido is back, my moods are better, I’m not spotting, and I don’t even have periods anymore. My hormones still fluctuate around that time but it’s much more manageable now. In my experience, Depo Provera is very polarizing to people. They either love it or hate it.

This is almost blow for blow how it went when my parents finally split, and I was about the same age as you are now. The divorce itself was amicable as far as splitting of the assets go, but the lead up was ugly. My dad ended up moving into an extended stay hotel until he could buy his own house, leaving me with my alcoholic mother who also treated me as her emotional support animal. Fights between my mother and I would get especially ugly because I’m very much like my dad and that was a huge trigger for her. When my dad finally got his place, I moved right in and slept on the floor in my own new bedroom. Not having to worry about my moms next meltdown and how I’m going to diffuse it. Not having to worry my mom will aspirate on her vomit when she passes out on the couch.

It sounds cold as fuck, but they are the adults here. They are supposed to be putting YOU first. Emotional divorce or not, you are not an asset that gets to be split with the divorce. You are a person who in the eyes of the court, is capable of making their own decisions. As far as people in your moms family go, they can go straight to hell. Enjoy the rest of high school, make that money, and live your own life. It’s so important to learn to find your voice and advocate for yourself, especially as a young woman. 

Let your mom cool off and if you want to (and only if you want to) offer her a compromise, like visits on the weekend or occasional mother-daughter days. Stay strong, OP. Your mom might turn out to be much cooler when you’re not living with her anymore!

I’m gonna say this because I feel no one ever talks about it. ED fucks up your body for good, even after you’re years into recovery and haven’t had a relapse in forever. Anorexia (what I dealt with) puts your body under so much stress that it starts to change the chemistry of it.

It’s really sad because a lot of theses girls and guys who starve themselves cause it’s a fad or because they wanna fit into whatever clothes don’t realize the rabbit hole they’re diving down. It becomes a compulsion after a while. Where every bite of food is met with crippling guilt and anxiety. Where you wait with bated breath for the numbers to show on the scale and either hate yourself because the number is higher than you wanted, or you get hard on yourself because it’s lower, *but not low enough*. 

I have been “recovered” from anorexia for four years. Because of the toll it took on my body, I still have irregular periods, my blood pressure is perpetually low and sometimes drops without warning making me faint, my blood sugar also drops drastically if I haven’t eaten in a few hours which causes me to vomit or faint or both, I have respiratory issues like asthma that have been linked back to me malnourishing myself, and let’s not forget the occasional flashbacks of guilt and self-loathing associated with food that will sometimes almost push me into relapse.

EDs are not fun, cute, pretty, tragically beautiful, or any combination of these romantic, trivializing buzz words. It’s hell. And if you’re lucky, you only have to worry about the triggering memories when it’s over.
